headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Authelia can broker auth while Dexter handles financial data and autonomous API calls, creating default-path exposure and unverified downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not provable. However, Authelia can pass through OIDC/ForwardAuth flows while Dexter uses autonomous execution and file scratchpads, so if operators bridge them via copied outputs or shared files, instruction hijacking becomes plausible. The pairwise pathway is indirect and not default.
conditions: IF the operator copies Authelia-generated text into Dexter prompts or scratchpads
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or message queue
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste bridges between auth logs and agent prompts
Add a manual review step before Dexter consumes any Authelia output
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial and market data and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/ForwardAuth. In a shared workspace or shared principal setup, sensitive data can flow from Dexter into Authelia-mediated auth paths or external services. The interaction is plausible in default deployments, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents run under the same OS account or shared workspace
IF Dexter scratchpad contents are accessible to Authelia-connected processes
mitigations: Separate the filesystem roots for the two agents
Restrict Authelia egress to required IdP endpoints only
Store Dexter scratchpads outside any shared auth workspace
Rotate and scope API keys per agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but only Dexter is documented with autonomous execution and multiple instances; Authelia is not shown to write shared mutable state. There is no evidence of overlapping filesystem or git writes, so direct capability conflict is limited unless operators co-locate them on the same mutable resources.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable directory
IF an orchestrator lets both modify the same external resource without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid shared git working trees
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
requires-engineering: add resource locks for shared targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution and API-heavy workflow make it likely to act on upstream outputs, while Authelia can emit authentication decisions or forwarded identity context. If Dexter consumes Authelia-derived results without verification, a mistaken auth or identity signal can cascade into incorrect financial-research actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Dexter treats Authelia output as authoritative input
IF Authelia-derived identity or access decisions are forwarded into Dexter workflows without validation
mitigations: Require a human check before Dexter acts on auth-derived inputs
Log and diff Authelia outputs before reuse
Add schema validation on any transferred fields
Limit Dexter to read-only analysis for auth-sensitive inputs
requires-engineering: implement provenance and verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly processes financial and market data and uses multiple third-party APIs, while Authelia provides authentication/ForwardAuth and broad egress. If regulated financial data or identity data is routed through both, retention, residency, or processor obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is sent through Dexter’s third-party APIs
IF identity or access logs from Authelia are retained alongside Dexter research data
mitigations: Minimize regulated data sent to third-party APIs
Separate auth logs from research logs
Set short retention windows for both systems
Review vendor DPAs before enabling shared workflows
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
